purpose: Prochlorperazine is mainly used to relieve nausea and vomiting, including nausea from surgery, cancer treatment, or migraines. It can also be used to treat anxiety and symptoms of certain mental health conditions like schizophrenia. Your doctor may prescribe it for severe nausea when other treatments have not worked well enough.
how_it_works: This medicine works by blocking certain chemical messengers in your brain, particularly one called dopamine. By blocking these signals, it helps calm the part of your brain that triggers the urge to vomit. It also helps balance other brain chemicals, which is why it can help with anxiety and some psychiatric symptoms.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or feeling sleepy, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, and low blood pressure when standing up quickly. Some people may notice restlessness, muscle stiffness, or unusual movements, especially of the face or limbs. These movement-related effects should be reported to your doctor right away.
warnings: This medication can cause serious movement disorders called extrapyramidal symptoms — tell your doctor immediately if you notice uncontrolled muscle movements or spasms. It should not be used in elderly patients with dementia-related conditions due to increased risk of serious events. Avoid alcohol and driving until you know how this medicine affects you. It can lower your seizure threshold and may cause a rare but dangerous condition called Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome, which causes high fever and muscle rigidity — seek emergency care if this happens.
typical_dosing: For nausea and vomiting in adults, a typical dose is 5 to 10 mg taken by mouth 3 to 4 times a day as needed. It can also be given as an injection in a medical setting. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on your condition and response. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and do not take more than prescribed.
